headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API document ingestion can feed untrusted content into Airflow-style automation, but no shared write surface or direct data residency breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP Server and processes PDFs/DOCX/XLSX content; Airflow is an automation orchestrator with broad network egress. A plausible pairwise pathway is untrusted document text flowing from MinerU into Airflow-managed workflows, where instructions could be misread as data or tasks. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into Airflow task parameters or DAG inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP or API bridge forwards document text from MinerU to Airflow as instructions, the attack path exists.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of raw MinerU text into Airflow task prompts.
Add a strict allowlist parser for MinerU outputs before any orchestration step.
Require human review for any document-derived instructions before DAG execution.
Log and flag any payload containing imperative language or tool directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from MinerU through Airflow pipelines.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while MinerU reads local documents and can expose them through API/MCP surfaces. However, the profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or sensitive data classes, so leakage is plausible but bounded. The main concern is accidental forwarding of document contents, not confirmed exfiltration.
conditions: IF the same local documents are mounted into both agents, MinerU content can be forwarded onward by Airflow.
IF Airflow tasks transmit MinerU-derived artifacts to external services, document leakage can occur.
mitigations: Keep MinerU inputs in a separate directory from Airflow workspaces.
Turn off any Airflow task that uploads document contents externally.
Review API destinations for any MinerU-derived payloads.
Use redaction on document text before passing it between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU explicitly has write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and execute_shell false, while Airflow’s profile does not show filesystem write or git mutation. With no overlapping mutable write surface documented, a direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The pair may coordinate, but the profiles do not support a write-write collision claim.
conditions: IF Airflow is deployed with additional filesystem-write operators not shown in the profile, conflict risk could change.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts where possible.
Avoid granting Airflow write access to MinerU input directories.
Separate any mutable state by directory or bucket.
Audit deployment manifests for hidden write permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, OCR, and formulas; Airflow is an automation system that can act on downstream outputs. If Airflow consumes MinerU results without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect pipeline actions. The profiles do not prove direct automation of side effects, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Airflow uses MinerU extraction as authoritative input for downstream tasks, errors can propagate.
IF no validation step checks OCR or table extraction before orchestration, cascading failure is possible.
mitigations: Insert validation checks between MinerU output and Airflow tasks.
Require confidence thresholds for OCR/table extraction before use.
Sample and manually review a subset of extracted records.
Quarantine low-confidence outputs from automated DAGs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and reconciliation jobs.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Airflow’s docs-only profile and MinerU’s open-source profile do not establish a compliance breach pathway by themselves. Because the relevant compliance attributes are absent, the safest supported verdict is none.
conditions: IF either deployment is later configured to process regulated data classes, this assessment must be revisited.
IF a residency or retention policy is added outside the profiles, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Document the data classes each pipeline may process.
Keep regulated data out of this pair unless reviewed.
Add retention rules before enabling sensitive workloads.
Review deployment regions and storage locations.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
